proposed statement: The client's current process for calculating advance payments to growers involves a spreadsheet that requires manual entry and reconciliation with the bank, causing delays in payment statements.
key statement: Sipho's spreadsheet has a row per delivery and is used to calculate monthly advance payments per carton of class one and two and per bin of juice, with a final pool payment once a year in February; payments go out via a bank batch file and the totals are journalled into LedgerOne monthly.

proposed statement: The client needs a system to automate the calculation of advance payments to growers based on delivery data and grader reports to reduce delays in payment statements.
key statement: Sipho's spreadsheet has a row per delivery and is used to calculate monthly advance payments per carton of class one and two and per bin of juice, with a final pool payment once a year in February; payments go out via a bank batch file and the totals are journalled into LedgerOne monthly.

proposed statement: The client needs a system to automate the calculation of advance payments to growers based on delivery data and grader reports to reduce delays in payment statements.
key statement: Growers' statements are made in the spreadsheet, printed and posted or emailed, and reach them about three weeks or more after the month ends, because everything is typed, checked and reconciled first.

proposed statement: The client needs a system to automate the generation of payment statements for growers to reduce the delay in payment statements from three weeks to a shorter timeframe.
key statement: Growers' statements are made in the spreadsheet, printed and posted or emailed, and reach them about three weeks or more after the month ends, because everything is typed, checked and reconciled first.

proposed statement: The client's current process for handling the seasonal cycle of citrus packing involves manual data entry and waiting for the optical grader to process fruit batches, causing delays in the pack out process.
key statement: Bosveld Citrus packs oranges (Valencias and navels), lemons and mandarins for its member growers, from large commercial farms to small growers with five or six hectares, through one packhouse in Letsitele; the season runs from the end of March (early mandarins) to about mid-September (last Valencias).

proposed statement: The client needs a system to automate the seasonal cycle of citrus packing to reduce delays in the pack out process.
key statement: At the weighbridge, WeighMate prints the truck's weight on a slip and the clerk copies it onto a handwritten three-copy carbon delivery ticket with the grower number, farm, orchard block, cultivar and number of bins; bins get a cardboard tag with the ticket number.

proposed statement: The system should use barcodes or QR codes for bin tracking to prevent misidentification due to cardboard tags falling off
key statement: How will bins be labelled for scanning? Most bins belong to the growers, some numbered and some not; the co-op lends out about 3,000 of its own bins with numbers burnt in; Precious floated a clip-on plastic barcode tag that comes back to the weighbridge, and the consultant will look into what other packhouses do.

proposed statement: The current system uses manual ticketing with handwritten tickets at the waybridge and cardboard tags for bin identification
key statement: Growers' bins get mixed up when cardboard tags fall off or ticket numbers are misread, two or three times a week in the peak, and each case takes a day to sort out.

proposed statement: The waybridge must work offline and catch up when the network is restored
key statement: Intake at the weighbridge must keep working without the network and catch up when the link is back; trucks can never be stopped at the gate.

proposed statement: The new system will provide deliveries and pack-out data as an export for Sypho's spreadsheet, not calculate payments
key statement: Do statements come from the new system (with Sipho uploading the advances each month) or stay in the spreadsheet?

proposed statement: Growers have varying phone usage, with some relying on family members for phone tasks
key statement: Growers' pages must work on cheap Android phones over slow connections without using much data, as a web page opened from a link (savable to the home screen), not an app to download.

proposed statement: The system must be designed to avoid additional app downloads for growers
key statement: Growers' pages must work on cheap Android phones over slow connections without using much data, as a web page opened from a link (savable to the home screen), not an app to download.

proposed statement: Growers change phone numbers, so the system must update phone numbers through the office like bank details
key statement: Bank details, and growers' phone numbers, are changed only by the office (bank details by Sipho with a letter from the bank), never by the grower from their phone, after an attempted fraud last year.

proposed statement: The system should be in English with possible zitsonga and afrikaans translations for grower pages, but the cost of adding these languages needs to be checked
key statement: Should the grower pages also be in Xitsonga (and perhaps Afrikaans)? English is the minimum, and statements must be in English for the auditors; the consultant will price the translation.

proposed statement: The client needs to split one truck's weight across several growers by their number of bins without weighing each bin individually
key statement: One truck can carry several growers' bins (a contractor collects from six or seven small growers); intake splits the truck's net weight across growers by number of bins, and each grower's ticket shows his share. The contractor, paid by the growers directly, needs nothing from the system.

proposed statement: The system must capture deliveries at the Weybridge in under a minute for the clerk to process
key statement: Capturing a delivery should take the clerk under a minute (it takes four to five minutes now, and the queue backs up onto the road).

proposed statement: The system must handle up to 2,400 bins per day during peak season
key statement: At the peak, 60 to 70 trucks a day, mostly between 07:00 and 11:00, carrying 6 to 40 bins each; 2,400 bins on the peak day last season and about 1,800 on a normal mid-season day.

proposed statement: The system must handle up to 1,800 bins per day during normal season
key statement: At the peak, 60 to 70 trucks a day, mostly between 07:00 and 11:00, carrying 6 to 40 bins each; 2,400 bins on the peak day last season and about 1,800 on a normal mid-season day.

proposed statement: The client needs to manage a growing number of growers with up to 162 members
key statement: Up to 162 member growers would use the portal (140 delivered last season; the others can come back any time), and the big farms have several users each (owner, manager, perhaps a bookkeeper), so a few hundred users at most.

proposed statement: The system must provide a daily summary for management showing bins received and packout per cultivar
key statement: A daily summary for management of the previous day's bins received and packout per cultivar, emailed at 06:00 and on a page Johan can look at, also when he is away.

proposed statement: The system must send a daily email summary to management at six in the morning
key statement: A daily summary for management of the previous day's bins received and packout per cultivar, emailed at 06:00 and on a page Johan can look at, also when he is away.

proposed statement: The client needs a daily summary for management that includes bins received and packout per cultivar for the previous day
key statement: A daily summary for management of the previous day's bins received and packout per cultivar, emailed at 06:00 and on a page Johan can look at, also when he is away.

proposed statement: The client needs a monthly report for the board that includes volumes, packout, and advances paid
key statement: The board's monthly report (volumes, packout, advances paid), which takes Sipho a day by hand, stays in his spreadsheet in phase one, with the volumes and packout coming from the system.

proposed statement: The client currently uses a spreadsheet for manual monthly reports
key statement: The board's monthly report (volumes, packout, advances paid), which takes Sipho a day by hand, stays in his spreadsheet in phase one, with the volumes and packout coming from the system.

proposed statement: The client wants the weighbridge system to be operational by the 1st of March 2027
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The client wants the grower pages to be available by the end of April 2027
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The client prefers the report to be laid out per grower, per cultivar, per class for the month with totals and delivery numbers
key statement: A monthly export for Sipho's spreadsheet with totals per grower, per cultivar and per class, with the delivery numbers alongside, not one row per bin.

proposed statement: The client's weighbridge clerks are comfortable with computers but the tipper staff are less comfortable
key statement: At the weighbridge, a rugged tablet rather than the PC, with big buttons usable with gloves and a screen readable in the sun; at the tipper, as close to one button as possible.

proposed statement: The client's weighbridge clerks are comfortable with computers but the tipper staff are less comfortable
key statement: Packhouse users: two weighbridge clerks (one per shift, both together in the peak) and three tipper staff over the shifts, plus Precious and the foreman; the clerks are comfortable with WhatsApp and the WeighMate screen, the tipper staff less so.

proposed statement: The Weybridge intake system must be live by March 1, 2027, to support the export process
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The grower pages must be available by the end of April to support the export process
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The system must mark deliveries as not for export when spray records are missing
key statement: Do the auditors accept digital spray records? Johan will ask them; their next audit is in May.

proposed statement: The client expects the grower pages to be available on Saturdays for growers to check their numbers
key statement: In the season the grower pages must be up on working days including Saturdays (the packhouse works Saturday mornings in the peak, when growers have time to look); an hour down is acceptable, a day is not. The consultant proposed 06:00 to 18:00, Monday to Saturday, with maintenance at night or out of season.

proposed statement: The client currently checks packouts manually, which creates a bottleneck as they review 60 batches per day
key statement: Does the grower see the packout straight from the grader, or only after Precious has checked the report (which would make her a bottleneck at about 60 batches a day in the peak)?

proposed statement: The system should send a warning when a vehicle's empty weight is more than a month old, to prevent payment errors
key statement: The system keeps each vehicle's empty weight and warns (not blocks) when it is more than a month old, so the clerk weighs that vehicle out and records the new tare; otherwise a grower can be paid for a heavier trailer.

proposed statement: When growers share a phone, does whoever has the phone see all of those growers or does each grower need his own number?
key statement: When several growers share one phone (for example the Mathebula family, three grower numbers on one phone), does whoever has the phone see all of them, or does each grower need his own number? Sipho will ask the lawyer member.

proposed statement: The system must allow growers to update their blocks with approval from office
key statement: Growers can propose changes to their orchard blocks (cultivar, planting year, hectares) on their page, and the office approves them, because the spray records follow the block; today the co-op finds out only when the wrong cultivar arrives.

proposed statement: Growers share phone numbers with multiple grower accounts
key statement: When several growers share one phone (for example the Mathebula family, three grower numbers on one phone), does whoever has the phone see all of them, or does each grower need his own number? Sipho will ask the lawyer member.

proposed statement: The system must show the growers' pages on their phones during study group days
key statement: If the small growers don't use the portal, the calls won't go down; mitigated by showing it at study group days and with the extension officer, Mister Baloyi, who visits every second week.

proposed statement: The extension officer visits small growers every second week
key statement: If the small growers don't use the portal, the calls won't go down; mitigated by showing it at study group days and with the extension officer, Mister Baloyi, who visits every second week.

proposed statement: The client has not yet determined who will handle day-to-day system administration tasks such as adding growers, clerks, and resetting tablets
key statement: Who at the co-op looks after the system day to day (adding growers and clerks, resetting tablets)? Perhaps Marietjie's replacement; Johan will come back on it before training.
